title: Power

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Work, Energy and Power

explanation: Power is the RATE at which work is done (or energy is transferred), P = W/t for average power over a time interval. Instantaneous power equals F·v·cosθ, the dot product of force and velocity — this is why the same amount of work done faster requires more power, even though the total energy transferred is identical. SI unit is the watt (1 W = 1 J/s); the commercial unit horsepower (1 hp ≈ 746 W) is also common for engines.

workedExample.scenario: A motor does 3000 J of work in 5 seconds.

commonMistakes: Confusing power (rate of doing work) with work/energy itself — power says nothing about total energy transferred, only how fast it's transferred.
Forgetting the cosθ term when computing instantaneous power from F and v that aren't in the same direction.
genZNote: Same work, less time, way more power — it's all about the hustle speed.
